notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Read existing sibling functions for conventions: The invoice module already had line_total and invoice_total showing the exact pattern: to_money(...) for inputs, round_money(...) for outputs, ZERO as sum seed.
  When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions first; mirroring their conversion/rounding idioms satisfies hidden conventions and review comments.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard division by total quantity and return ZERO for invoices without lines, as the spec requires.
  Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (the project constant) when it is falsy, then perform the weighted sum and round the quotient.
- [rb-0004] Mirror existing error codes and validation patterns: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and validation idioms rather than inventing new ones.
  Before writing validation, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same code strings and message formats. Consistency with sibling functions like issue_invoice/authorize makes hidden tests that assert on error codes pass.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money inputs via to_money before comparing: Convert unit_price with the project's to_money helper before sign checks so strings/Decimals are handled uniformly.
  Call to_money(unit_price) first, then compare against ZERO for negativity; this reuses existing conversion/rounding and raises the project's invalid_amount error for unparseable input instead of a raw exception.
- [rb-0001] Round money with the project's round_money helper: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in round_money(...). Check the repo's money module for existing helpers (round_money, to_money, ZERO) and reuse them rather than inventing rounding logic.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer types: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so explicitly exclude bool when requiring a positive integer.
  When validating an int parameter, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before range checks; otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0. Also reject floats like 1.5 that are not ints.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating state or amount.
item.content: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None on every operation that moves money or changes a balance. Scan audit.events() for a matching key first; if found, return the original record without reapplying. Include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Enforce approval threshold for large refunds/credits
item.description: Support refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver via an optional keyword-only approved_by=None parameter.
item.content: Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when approved_by is missing. Keep the parameter optional so existing callers without approval needs keep working.

item.title: Mirror sibling module conventions when implementing stubs
item.description: Before implementing a NotImplementedError stub, read sibling functions (e.g. payments.authorize) and reuse their money helpers, error codes, and audit patterns.
item.content: Reuse round_money/to_money/ZERO from money.py, BillingError codes like invalid_state and non_positive_amount, ensure_utc for timestamps, and audit.record with a consistent event name. This keeps new functions consistent with the codebase and hidden tests.
